exclude: runtime: the text screen, where the disk prompt at $0AA4 writes; what it holds in the snapshot is left from the boot
runtime: the unpacker's pair tables ($D100-$D3FF), built for each chunk, and its three 1 KB buffers ($D400-$DFFF)
11 parts: The title screen, Weightlifting, The travelogue and others
elsewhere: 11 parts: The title screen, Weightlifting, The travelogue and others

comments.text: the processor port's data direction register; the hardware reset at $0B54 sets it to $2F
the processor port: which ROMs and the I/O area are in view. The shell keeps $36 (BASIC out, KERNAL and I/O in) for the parts and $34 (all RAM) while it copies under the I/O area or unpacks
which side of the disk is in the drive, as a mask: 1 for side 1, 2 for side 2, found by $0AA4 from whether file R loads

the number of the part being loaded or run, times two: the index into every table from $0CA8 to $0CFC (0 menu, 2 travelogue, 4 title, 6 to 20 the eight events, 22 the unpacker C, 24 slalom's second file J, 26 the records R)
where $0BCC and the travelogue's detour keep $09 while they load another file
the address a file is loaded to, low byte; the high byte is $0C
the high byte of the load address
the one-letter name of the file to load, from $0CC4: SETNAM points the KERNAL at this byte
the source pointer of the copy of slalom's second file from $A000 to $E000, low byte; high byte $11
the copy's source page, $A0 to $BE
the copy's destination pointer, low byte; high byte $13
the copy's destination page, $E0 to $FE
the hardware reset at $0B54 clears $80-$FF, the zero page the parts use for their own variables
the unpacker's read pointer into the packed data of the current chunk, low byte; high byte $B1
the high byte of the unpacker's packed-data pointer
the unpacker's write pointer into the current buffer, low byte; high byte $B3
the high byte of the unpacker's write pointer: the buffer's page, $D4, $D8 or $DC
the unpacker's read pointer into the current chunk's pair table, low byte; high byte $B5
the high byte of the pair-table pointer
the current chunk's end code: the first byte of its pair table, which also marks the table's end and the packed data's end
the stack pointer as the expansion of one packed byte starts: the stack is empty again when it comes back to this
the offset of the current chunk's five-byte entry in the packed file's header at $1000; it starts at the last entry ($10FF) and falls by 5
counts the chunks from $FC: the buffers are not flushed until the fourth chunk, when it reaches 0
the page each of the three buffers is to be copied to, one byte each ($BA-$BC), when the buffer is flushed
which buffer the next chunk unpacks into: 2, 1, 0, 2, ...
the buffer flushed by the last loop of the unpacker, 2 down to 0
the unpacker's caller's return address, low byte, taken off the stack at $D000 and put back at the end; high byte $C0
the high byte of the caller's return address
the KERNAL's flag that lets shift and the Commodore key switch the character set; $80 locks it

the boot program, file "WORLD GAMES", 93 bytes loaded to $02A7-$0303. Loaded with ,8,1 it overwrites the BASIC main loop's vector at $0302 with $02B3 and starts itself; loaded to $0801 instead it is a BASIC line, SYS 2061, which reaches the same code
the boot's code: loads file L, the shell, to its own address $0900, with no messages, and jumps to the cold start at $0909. The name 'L' is written at $C000 for SETNAM
the rest of the boot file: zeros as far as the vector
the BASIC main loop's vector as the boot file sets it: $02B3, the boot's code
the KERNAL's interrupt, break and NMI vectors ($0314-$0319); $0B54 puts back the copy kept at $0D31
the NMI vector, low byte: set to $091A, so RUN/STOP-RESTORE goes to the shell's handler
the NMI vector's high byte
the KERNAL's STOP vector, low byte: set to $0B51, so the KERNAL never sees RUN/STOP during a load
the STOP vector's high byte
the screen row the disk prompt's first line goes to: row 10, column 7 of the screen at $0400
the screen row of the disk prompt's second line: row 12, column 7

the page of variables the parts share, $0800-$08FF: the cold start clears it, and the menu and the events keep the players and their results here; the variables the shell itself uses have names of their own
bit 7 set for practice, from the menu's practice option (the hidden credits screens set it to $FF as they leave): the events then show no attempt numbers and ask TRY AGAIN
the number of players, 1 to 8, from the registration
the event the menu asks the shell to load, 0 (weightlifting) to 7 (sumo)
bit 7 set when the menu is not in memory and must be loaded: $FF from the cold start and after every load ($0A7A); a restart ($09B5) jumps straight back into the menu when it is clear
the shell's resume address in the menu, low byte; the menu sets it before each load
the resume address's high byte: not zero when the menu should carry on where it was; cleared by the RUN/STOP-RESTORE handler at $091A as it abandons the games
not zero to load the part asked for even when it is already in memory: $FF from the cold start, cleared by every load
the number of joysticks, 1 or 2: 2 from the cold start, swapped by the menu's option; with one, the events that pair players set each against the computer
not zero to skip the travelogue before an event; zero, the default, shows it
the competition's events, a bit each, weightlifting (bit 7) to sumo (bit 0); $089E after it holds no event's bit
the number of the part last loaded at $1000, times two: $09C4 does not load it again while it is there
the menu's random generator: $08FD-$08FE shifted with feedback from their own low bits, $08FF a counter mixed in; log rolling starts its frame counter from the first two

the shell's jump table, at the same address for every part: $0900 restarts the games at the menu, $0903 loads and runs part X-1, $0906 saves the world records, $0909 is the cold start and $090C runs the part just unpacked
the jump table's second entry: load and run the part numbered X-1 ($090F)
the jump table's third entry: save the world records to the disk ($0A51)
the jump table's fourth entry: the cold start, where the boot program jumps ($0C44)
the jump table's fifth entry, where the unpacker ends: run the part ($0991)
loads and runs part X-1 for a part that called $0903: puts the machine back to its start-up state ($0B54), keeping X, and goes on at $09C4

the NMI handler, for the RESTORE key. With RUN/STOP held it abandons the games: sprites off, the screen blanked, every colour and colour RAM black, then the restart at $09B5 back to the menu. Without RUN/STOP it puts CIA 1's port directions back and returns. While a file loads its first byte is RTI ($0A62), so RESTORE does nothing then
selects keyboard column 7 alone (port A bit 7 the only output, driven low) and reads row 7 of it: RUN/STOP
RUN/STOP is held: A is 0 here
the end of the cold start: loads the world records, file R, to $0E00, then the title (part 2)
'R', the name of the world records file; $0AA4 also loads it to tell the disk's sides apart
runs the part numbered $09: takes its entry address from $0CFC into the JMP at $09B2, ROMs set to $36, waits until the raster line's low eight bits are below 128, blanks the screen and jumps there
the low byte of the JMP's target: $0991 writes the part's entry address here
the high byte of the JMP's target

restarts the games at the menu (from $0900 and the RUN/STOP-RESTORE handler): empties the stack, resets the machine's chips ($0B54) and runs part 0, the menu, at once if it is still in memory ($083D), otherwise loading it first

loads and runs part X (0 menu, 1 travelogue, 2 title, 3-10 the events). A part already at $1000 is run as it is. Otherwise it loads the unpacker ($0BCC); before an event, unless the travelogue is off ($087F), it first loads, unpacks and runs the travelogue, which returns here; then the part's file is loaded and unpacked, and the unpacker ends at $090C, which runs it. Slalom (part 6) also needs file J, copied to $E000 first

before an event: keep its number, load the travelogue (part 1) and unpack and run it as a subroutine; when it returns, reset the chips, set the character set at $1800 ($D018 = $17), take the event's number back and load the unpacker again
load the part's file; for slalom, load J to $A000 too and copy its 31 pages to $E000-$FEFF under the KERNAL
unpacks the file just loaded at $1000 into its places: all RAM in view ($01 = $34), the chunk counter at $FC, the last header entry's offset from $10FF, three buffers, then the unpacker at $D000
saves the world records ($0E00-$0EFF) to the disk as file R, over the old one: asks for side 1 if the other side is in the drive ($0AA4 with file R's number, 26), then sets $09 to 6

loads file number $09 from the disk to its address in $0CE0: RESTORE is turned off for the load ($091A = RTI), CIA 2's timer A is started for 32 cycles, one-shot; asks for the right side of the disk first ($0AA4); afterwards RESTORE comes back, CIA 2's interrupt flags are read, which clears them, and the ROMs are set to $36

makes sure the file numbered $09 is on the side of the disk in the drive. It loads file R to $C000: if that fails it is side 2. When the file's sides mask in $0CA9 says it is not there, it puts "INSERT WORLD GAMES SIDE #n" and "THEN PRESS JOYSTICK BUTTON" on the screen in white, the rest of colour RAM blue, switches the screen on, waits for fire on either joystick and looks again
the side wanted: '0' plus the position of the mask's lowest set bit, counted from 1, into the prompt at $0B36
waits for the fire button on either joystick: bit 4 of both of CIA 1's ports
the file is on this side: blank the screen and return
"INSERT WORLD GAMES SIDE #", with the side's digit written over the # at $0B36; stored straight into screen memory
the disk prompt's side digit: '1' or '2' once $0ACC has written it
"THEN PRESS JOYSTICK BUTTON", the disk prompt's second line
the KERNAL's STOP routine for the whole game ($0328): A = $FF with the zero flag clear, as if RUN/STOP were never pressed, so a load is never broken off

puts the machine back to its start-up state between parts: interrupts off, decimal mode off, the screen blanked, the vectors from $0D31, the processor port ($2F, $36), every CIA interrupt off, CIA 1's port A all outputs at $FF and port B all inputs, the three SID voices silenced (test bit) and the filter's cutoff and resonance cleared, the VIC's sprite, interrupt and colour registers cleared ($D000-$D010, $D019-$D03A), sprites off, the background colours 6, 2 and 1, VIC bank 0, and zero page $80-$FF cleared
loads the unpacker, file C, to $0F00 and copies its 256 bytes to $D000, under the I/O area, where it runs; keeps $09 in $0A meanwhile
the SID voice settings the reset gives each voice ($D400-$D406, $D407-$D40D, $D40E-$D414): frequency 0, pulse 0, control $08 (the test bit, which silences the voice), envelope 0
the background colours $0B54 sets: $D021 = 6 (blue), $D022 = 2, $D023 = 1
loads the file whose one-letter name is at $0F from device 8 to the address in $0B/$0C, through the KERNAL: no messages, secondary address 0 (to the address given)
saves $0E00-$0EFF as "@0:R" on device 8, the @0: replacing the old file

the game's start, from the boot program: ROMs $36; the three SID voices set to noise at frequency $0F0F with the volume at 0; $0800-$08FF cleared, then $083D and $085F set to $FF and $087D to 2; the NMI vector (at $0318 and at $FFFA, for when the KERNAL is out) to $091A, the STOP vector to $0B51; the vectors saved at $0D31; the sprites' positions to $58, which the reset straight after sets to 0; the shift and Commodore keys' character set switch locked; the chips reset; then the records and the title ($097B)
"@0:R", the name $0C1B saves the records under
a zero no instruction reads

two bytes for each file, by $09: the odd byte ($0CA9 + $09) is the disk sides it is on, 1 side 1, 2 side 2, $0F either (the menu, travelogue and unpacker are on both); the even byte, which nothing reads, is within three of the file's length in 256-byte pages
the first file's sides mask: $0CA9 + $09 is the byte $0AA4 reads, and so the odd bytes of the table at $0CA8 are the masks

each file's one-letter name, by $09: B menu, H travelogue, A title, F weightlifting, E barrel jumping, G cliff diving, I slalom, M log rolling, K bull riding, O caber toss, N sumo, C unpacker, J slalom's second file, R records; a space between each
each file's load address, by $09: $1000 for the parts, $0F00 for the unpacker, $A000 for J, $0E00 for the records
the high bytes of the load addresses, read with $0CE1 + $09
each part's entry address, by $09: $1000, except slalom's at $8000; the last three, for the files that are not parts, are not used
the high bytes of the entry addresses, read with $0CFD + $09

what the cold start writes to the SID's registers, $D400-$D41C: each voice noise ($81, gate on) at frequency $0F0F and pulse $0F0F, attack-decay and sustain-release $0F, filter and volume 0. Voice 3 left running as noise makes $D41B a source of random numbers. The last four go to read-only registers, from the first bytes of $0D31
the interrupt, break and NMI vectors ($0314-$0319) as the cold start leaves them, NMI at $091A: $0B54 puts them back every time

the world records, file R, read from the disk by the cold start and saved by $0A51: one record of 20 bytes for each event in turn, the name (10 characters), a space and the result as it is shown (6), and three bytes of the result as a number. This disk image's records are not blank: eight entries with names such as FREDDE and POLIZEI. $0EA0-$0EFF is empty
file C as loaded: the unpacker, which $0BCC copies to $D000 and which runs there; its last nine bytes, past the table at $D0F4, are not read

unpacks the file loaded at $1000. The file starts with a header of five-byte entries, one for each chunk of up to 1 KB: the chunk's pair table, its packed data and the page it goes to. Each chunk is expanded in turn, last first, into one of three buffers under the I/O area ($D400, $D800, $DC00), and a buffer is copied to its destination three chunks later, so a chunk never overwrites packed data still to be read. Then the last three are copied, and it jumps to $090C, which runs the part

the next chunk: its packed data to $B0, its pair table to $B4, the next buffer in turn, the destination of what that buffer holds to $D0DF and the chunk's own destination in its place; from the fourth chunk on, that buffer is copied out first ($D0D6)
the last copies: the three buffers still held, to their destinations

expands one chunk into the buffer at $B2/$B3. Its pair table starts with the chunk's end code ($B6); every three bytes after it give one byte a meaning as a pair of others, until the end code again; up to 255 pairs. Then each packed byte is written out as it is, unless it has a pair, which is pushed on the stack second half first and expanded in turn: byte pair encoding. The end code ends the packed data
the next packed byte, until the end code
expands one byte: a byte with a pair is replaced by its first half, the second waiting on the stack; one without is written out, then the next waiting byte, if any
the next byte of the pair table at $B4, which steps on
copies a buffer, four pages from page $D0DC, to page $D0DF on: both are the operands of the copy loop, which stops when the destination reaches page $CE, so nothing is copied to $CE00 or above
the copy's source page, written at $D03C and $D05A and stepped by the loop
the copy's destination page, written at $D02B and $D054 and stepped by the loop: the next instructions step both pages and stop at page $CE or after four pages
the three buffers' pages, $D4, $D8 and $DC
the NMI vector in the RAM under the KERNAL, set to $091A by the cold start for when the parts bank the KERNAL out
